fields.why: Table 1 note says VE was 'Manufacturer-calculated efficacy based on hazard ratios', which implies a proportional-hazards model; B recorded the event-time outcome from the same note but not the model, while both readers record methods behind other cited estimates (the IRR's CI inversion).
Hazard ratios map to the event-time family; the model is unnamed, which A states in inferred_from.
Follows from the hazard-ratio model behind Table 1's VE; the other classes are agreed.

Besides the pairwise vaccine-vs-placebo and risk-vs-control-interval contrasts, Table 1 sets VE across four follow-up periods and Table 2 sets benefit-risk across three age/risk groups for each product; the brief says to use group when pair and group coexist.

Rurality appears as a descriptor framed as access ('remote or rural community where transportation ... is challenging'), which is level 1 by rule; B recorded the same rurality descriptor yet scored 0.

Transportation barriers to escalation of care in rural or remote areas are offered as the reason that residence raises risk of severe RSV disease (a structural explanation of an outcome); reading it as a clinical risk factor in a box, as B did, is also defensible.

Table 2's three groups cross a two-level SPD (≥75 vs 60–74 years) with clinical status, which is not an SPD, so no three-group SPD set exists; A noted this itself but still made an entry. Rule needed: groups formed by crossing an SPD with a non-SPD variable count only by their SPD levels.
Once the hazard model is recorded, regression_fields must be filled; nothing is stated about nonindependence, so 'none' with ev [] is acceptable.
The manufacturer model's covariates are not given, so the methods are too sketchy to tell; null is acceptable under the brief.
Same as unadjusted: the covariates of the cited model are not reported.
No interaction term or test is reported; the default is false.
The follow-up windows in Table 1 are the waning comparison rather than a re-analysis, so the default false holds.

brief_issues: Two gaps: whether methods behind estimates only cited in an ACIP summary (manufacturer HRs, FDA SCCS IRR) are recorded as procedures; and how to count groupwise groups formed by crossing an SPD with a clinical variable.
